contamination_rule_quote: PLAN.md 5.1: "Per-date empirical check (real, uninjected data, not just calendar proximity) - swap only where an actual effect exists, not just proximity." PLAN.md 8 (holiday screening gap row): "A date can pass its pass condition for the wrong reason, not just fail for the wrong reason; a contamination check needs to look for both."
method: Bipartite max-matching (Kuhn/DFS augmenting paths, hand-implemented, no networkx dependency), not greedy. Each of the 8 non-I3b incidents is represented by k interchangeable slots; edges connect a slot to a date iff that date survived the incident's own eligibility+contamination filters AND is not I3b's single reserved date. Slots are processed in a fixed (incident, replica-index) order; each slot's candidate dates are iterated in the order they appear in the single numpy default_rng(SEED)-shuffled date sequence, so the seed - not insertion order or dict/set iteration - decides which valid dates are picked whenever more than one feasible assignment exists. k starts at 9 and drops to 8, then 7, stopping at the first value for which every slot can be matched to a distinct date (a perfect matching on the slot side).
